prompt:
A flat, matte design sketch of a desktop website homepage, landscape 16:9, shown straight on with no perspective, no device frame, no browser chrome, no drop shadows, no gloss, no photorealism. Deliberately unfinished, like a designer's layout study rendered in flat color blocks.

Palette, used exactly: warm aged-paper off-white background (#F7F3ED), dark warm ink (#2A231C), one muted slate blue accent (#365778), and a deep near-black warm brown (#171310) used for a few solid blocks. No other colors. A faint regular dot grid over the paper background.

The page is one dense composed wall of overlapping screenshot panels, like a printed poster or a contact sheet, not a tidy grid of equal cards. It should feel abundant and deliberately arranged.

Composition:

Across the whole canvas, arrange roughly nine to twelve rectangular panels of clearly different sizes, tiled and slightly overlapping, filling the frame edge to edge with only small paper gaps showing between them. Each panel has a thin dark hairline border. Vary them:

- Two or three large panels filled with soft indistinct horizontal lines of varying length, standing in for pages of prose. These are the biggest panels.
- Two small panels that are solid dark warm brown blocks with a few faint indistinct lines over them, standing in for world images.
- Two narrow tall panels laid out like a form or record sheet: a short heading line, then rows of paired short lines with small squared markers to their right, standing in for character sheets.
- One panel showing three stacked rounded rectangles of equal size, standing in for a list of choices, with the middle one filled solid slate blue.
- One small panel that is mostly empty paper with a single short line and a small bracketed marker.
- One panel filled with many short lines in two columns, standing in for a journal.

Layered on top of this wall, in the upper left, a large serif headline on a solid block of the paper color so it stays readable over the panels, reading exactly: Play a story in any world you can imagine

Directly under the headline, one short greeked line and one solid slate-blue rectangular button. This button is the single strongest colored element in the whole image.

The word Narraitor appears once, small, in a thin header strip across the very top.

Apart from the word Narraitor and the headline, absolutely no legible text anywhere: every other text region is greeked, soft indistinct horizontal lines standing in for words, not real letters. Do not render invented prices, dates, statistics, logos, faces, or photographs.

The overall feeling is a densely packed printed poster of specimens on good paper: a lot of real material shown at once, arranged with care.
